==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:populer|text=++|tree=1}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈpɒp.jʊ.lə/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈpɑ.pjə.lɚ/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-popular.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɒpjələ(ɹ)|s=3}} * {{hyph|en|pop|u|lar}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj}} # [[common|Common]] among the [[general public]]; generally [[accept]]ed. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|author=Joe Queenan|journal=The Guardian|date=23 Aug 2007 |passage=Contrary to '''popular''' misconception, MacArthur Park is not the worst song ever written.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7132598/|title=Caffeine induces neurobehavioral effects through modulating neurotransmitters|work={{w|lang=de|Saudi Pharmaceutical Journal}}|author= Fawaz Alasmari|date=2020-02-17|volume=28|issue=4|pages=445–451|doi=10.1016/j.jsps.2020.02.005|passage=Recent evidence demonstrates that caffeine addiction is becoming '''popular''' worldwide.}} # {{lb|en|legal}} Concerning the people; [[public]]. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} # Pertaining to or deriving from the [[people]] or general public. {{defdate|from 16th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1594|author=w:Richard Hooker|title=Preface |passage=At the coming of Calvin thither, the form of their civil regiment was '''popular''', as it continueth at this day: neither king, nor duke, nor nobleman of any authority or power over them, but officers chosen by the people out of themselves, to order all things with public consent.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=w:Diarmaid MacCulloch|title=A History of Christianity|page=645|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2010 |passage=Luther in '''popular''' memory had become a saint, his picture capable of saving houses from burning down, if it was fixed to the parlour wall.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2009|author=Graham Smith|journal=The Guardian|section=letter, 27 May 2009 |passage=Jonathan Freedland brilliantly articulates the size and nature of the challenge and we must take his lead in setting out a radical agenda for a new republic based on the principle of '''popular''' sovereignty.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Of [[low]] [[birth]], not [[noble]]; [[vulgar]], [[plebian]]. {{defdate|16th|17th c.}} #* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=17|book=II|passage='''Popular''' and shallow-headed mindes, cannot perceive the grace or comelinesse, nor judge of a smooth and quaint discourse.}} # [[aim|Aimed]] at [[ordinary]] people, as opposed to [[specialist]]s etc.; intended for general [[consumption]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=8 Apr 2009|title=Meltdown |passage=As a work of '''popular''' science it is exemplary: the focus may be the numbers, but most of the mathematical legwork is confined to the appendices and the accompanying commentary is amusing and witty, as well as informed.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Cultivating the favour of the common people. {{defdate|16th|18th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1712|author=w:Joseph Addison|title=Cato, A Tragedy |passage=Such '''popular''' humanity is treason.}} # [[like|Liked]] by many people; generally [[pleasing]], widely [[admire]]d. {{defdate|from 17th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=w:Edwin Black |chapter=2|title=[http://openlibrary.org/works/OL4103950W Internal Combustion] |passage=The '''popular''' late Middle Ages fictional character Robin Hood, dressed in green to symbolize the forest, dodged fines for forest offenses and stole from the rich to give to the poor. But his appeal was painfully real and embodied the struggle over wood.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2 Oct 2011|journal=The Observer |passage=They might have split 24 years ago, but the Smiths remain as '''popular''' as ever, and not just among those who remember them first time around.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-03 |author=David S. Senchina|volume=101|issue=2|page=134|magazine=w:American Scientist |title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/2/athletics-and-herbal-supplements Athletics and Herbal Supplements] |passage=Athletes' use of herbal supplements has skyrocketed in the past two decades. At the top of the list of '''popular''' herbs are echinacea and ginseng, whereas garlic, St. John's wort, soybean, ephedra and others are also surging in popularity or have been historically prevalent.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160715135921/http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/2/athletics-and-herbal-supplements/1}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Helen Regan, Isaac Yee and Eve Brennan|title=Australian teens among six tourists dead as countries warn of suspected methanol poisonings in Laos|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/21/asia/australia-backpacker-dies-methanol-poisoning-laos-intl-hnk|date=2024-11-21|passage= The Australian teens, both from Melbourne, were enjoying a backpacking trip when they became ill after a night out in Vang Vieng.
The picturesque rural town in northern Laos has long been a '''popular''' backpacking spot.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260323125255/https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/21/asia/australia-backpacker-dies-methanol-poisoning-laos-intl-hnk|archivedate=23 March 2026}} # [[adapt|Adapted]] to the means of the common people; Earlier that day, in their feminist studies class, the women were discussing Nathaniel Hawthorne's The Scarlet Letter, a novel ...}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|in the plural}} An inexpensive [[newspaper]] with wide [[circulation]]. #* {{quote-book |en |year=1983 |author=Jeremy Tunstall |title=The Media in Britain |publisher=Columbia University Press |isbn=9780231058162 |page=75 |passage=Serious newspapers boomed; the '''populars''' became tabloid supplements to television, with the television schedules and related features increasingly the core of the newspaper.}} # A member of the {{w|Populares}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1843|author=Thucydides|title=“The” History of the Grecian War, Translated by Thomas Hobbes|page=415 |passage=[...] when their ambassadors were come from Samos, and that they saw not only the '''populars''', but also some others of their own party thought trusty before, to be now changed.}} ===References=== * {{R:OneLook}} * {{R:Keywords 21st}} * {{R:Keywords|page=236}} * {{R:Century}} * {{R:Webster 1913}} {{C|en|Ancient Rome}}
